extracted.intended_audience: philosophers of mathematics, graduate students, mathematicians, and interested non-specialists
extracted.subtask_description: Introductory and programmatic overview defining aims, traditions, and research questions for a philosophy of mathematical practice that emphasizes attention to mathematical practice, historical case studies, and methodological questions. Targets both pedagogical exposition and original research directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unify contributions informed by mathematical practice
rubrics_metrics.description: First aim: 'I wanted to unify the efforts of many philosophers who were making contributions to a philosophy of mathematics informed by a desire to account for many central aspects of mathematical practice that, by and large, had been ignored by previous philosophers and logicians.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work collected should bring together philosophers who focus on aspects of mathematical practice (visualization, explanation, diagram use, methods, etc.) rather than solely on foundational logic; the collection should represent a coherent, practice-informed research program rather than disparate standalone papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce a work useful to a wide audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Second aim: produce 'a book that would be useful to a large segment of the community, from interested undergraduates to specialists.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions should balance accessibility and depth: include material approachable by undergraduates and non-specialists while also containing research papers that advance the field for experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic selection representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The eight topics selected 'encompass much of contemporary philosophical reflection on key aspects of mathematical practice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select topics that together give a representative sample of the main contemporary concerns in philosophy of mathematical practice; ensure coverage of central themes such as visualization, explanation, diagrammatic reasoning, concepts, computers, and interaction with physics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-format organization: introductory chapter + research article
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational standard: 'Each topic is discussed in an introductory chapter and in a research article in the very same area.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pedagogical and research aims, pair an accessible overview that introduces the area with a more technical research contribution in that same area; introductory chapters should be general and accessible, research articles should push the field forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction should contextualize contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: The book's introduction aims 'to provide the context out of which, and sometimes against which, most of the contributions to the volume have originated' and 'to give a fair account of the landscape that could be useful also, but not only, to the non-initiated.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing material should explain traditions, tensions, and how contributions relate to one another and to wider debates; it should be intelligible to non-specialists while accurately reflecting scholarly background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to mathematical practice as necessary for renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim: 'attention to mathematical practice is a necessary condition for a renewal of the philosophy of mathematics' and that philosophy should address 'fruitfulness, evidence, visualization, diagrammatic reasoning, understanding, explanation, and other aspects of mathematical epistemology.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical work should engage with concrete practices of mathematicians and the epistemic phenomena arising from them (e.g., how visualization contributes to understanding), not restrict itself to abstract ontological access problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match philosophical problems to appropriate mathematical domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation: 'Certain philosophical problems become salient only when the appropriate area of mathematics is taken into consideration... geometry, knot theory, and algebraic topology are bound to awaken interest in... diagrammatic reasoning and visualization' and 'cohomology' exemplifies pervasive structural reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When investigating a philosophical question (e.g., diagram use, structuralism), choose mathematical case studies where that phenomenon is prominent; avoid drawing general conclusions from domains ill-suited to the issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maverick tradition features (methodological criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterization of the 'maverick' approach: (a) anti-foundationalism — 'there is no certain foundation for mathematics; mathematics is a fallible activity'; (b) anti-logicism — 'mathematical logic cannot provide the tools for an adequate analysis of mathematics and its development'; (c) attention to mathematical practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The maverick methodology values historical and practice-sensitive study of mathematics, treats mathematics as revisable and fallible, and resists seeing logic alone as the primary analytic tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy of 'real' mathematics criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Corfield's definition: 'The intention of this term is to draw a line between work informed by the concerns of mathematicians past and present and that done on the basis of at best token contact with its history or practice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical work should be grounded in substantial engagement with historical case studies and contemporary mathematical practice rather than superficial or purely foundational abstractions; avoid the 'foundationalist filter'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study goals for a philosophy of real mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Corfield proposes philosophy should examine 'what leading mathematicians of their day have achieved, how their styles of reasoning evolve, how they justify the course along which they steer their programmes, what constitute obstacles to their programmes, how they come to view a domain as worthy of study and how their ideas shape and are shaped by the concerns of physicists and other scientists.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should analyze mathematicians' reasoning styles, justificatory practices, research program dynamics, obstacles, domain formation, and interdisciplinary interactions (e.g., with physics). Use case studies to illuminate these issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate fruitfulness, connectivity, and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Corfield's motivating topics include: (1) 'Why are some mathematical entities important, natural, and fruitful while others are not?'; (2) 'What accounts for the connectivity of mathematics?'; (3) 'Why are computer proofs unable to provide the sort of understanding at which mathematicians aim?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical inquiry should provide accounts of conceptual fruitfulness, cross-field conceptual connections, and the epistemic role and limits of computational/formal proofs; empirical and historical study of examples is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance historical fidelity with theoretical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated theme: criticisms of approaches that ignore historical development or mathematicians' actual concerns; the need to combine historical case studies with theoretical/analytic work (e.g., Lakatos-style interplay of rational reconstruction and historical development).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodologies should integrate careful historical scholarship with normative or explanatory philosophical analysis; avoid purely schematic or ahistorical reconstructions disconnected from actual practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical + research dual aim for contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial policy: 'the aim of the introductory chapters is to provide a general and accessible overview of an area of research... The research papers obviously have the aim of pushing the field forwards.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors should write material serving both entry-level learners and advancing specialists: introductory exposition plus substantive new results or arguments.
